macro.narrative: The macro picture is shifting from a pure energy shock toward a yields-led, late-cycle risk-off. The real economy is still hot — May payrolls printed +172k (vs ~80-85k expected), unemployment 4.3%, Q2 GDP tracking ~3% — and that strong jobs report repriced the Fed hawkish, lifting the 10y to ~4.5% and the 30y near 5% while crushing gold to its lowest since March and sending Bitcoin to a 19-month low near $61k. On the geopolitical side the oil premium is deflating: after the April spike to a ~$138 Brent peak from the Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iran declared its operations over and a new ~60-day U.S.-brokered ceasefire is reportedly close, so even a brief June 8 exchange of strikes only spiked Brent above $97 intraday before it settled back to ~$94 (WTI ~$91); OPEC+ has now approved a fourth output hike (+188k b/d from July). The June 16-17 FOMC is ~95% priced for no change, leaving the May CPI report (due June 10) as the swing catalyst: a hot print revives the ~35-45% year-end hike pricing under new Chair Warsh, a benign one reopens cut hopes. With the S&P at a CAPE in the high-30s/low-40s, a near-zero equity risk premium and AI capex itself now feeding the inflation data, we stay modestly defensive — favoring cash/USD and still-structurally-bid real assets over richly priced equities and historically tight credit — but stop short of full risk-off given no recession or credit stress and a fading energy tail.

De-escalating: Iran declared operations over and a ~60-day ceasefire is reportedly close; a June 8 strike exchange spiked Brent >$97 intraday but it faded to ~$94. A signed, durable ceasefire is the dominant disinflationary/bullish catalyst; re-escalation is the tail risk.

The strong jobs report drove the 10y to ~4.5% and 30y near 5%, mechanically hitting long-duration equities, gold (lowest since March) and crypto (BTC 19-month low). A stronger dollar is compounding the squeeze on non-yielding assets.

S&P CAPE in the high-30s/low-40s with a near-zero equity risk premium; the top ~10 names are ~40% of the index and AI-buildout goods/services are now a visible contributor to CPI/PCE — leaving little cushion for an earnings or capex disappointment.
IG (~80bps) and HY (~285-300bps) sit near multi-decade tights against a record 2026 IG supply calendar, leaving minimal margin for error if growth wobbles or yields grind higher.

byAssetClass.note: Solid earnings (~24% EPS growth, Street targets ~7800-8000) and no recession argue up over 12m, but a record-low equity risk premium, a high-30s/low-40s CAPE, rising real yields and extreme AI concentration cap upside and fatten the downside tail; the 9-week win streak just broke with a -2.6% Friday.

Still the cleanest stagflation hedge — structural central-bank gold demand and a tight Q2 oil balance — but the call is downgraded to modest OW as Brent de-rates from ~$138 to ~$94 on ceasefire progress and a fourth OPEC+ hike; gold's jobs-driven slide to a March low adds near-term two-way risk.

BTC has slid to a ~19-month low near $61k on sustained ETF outflows, higher-for-longer rates and a stronger dollar; highest beta to liquidity makes it the first casualty if the yields/risk-off move extends, with genuinely two-sided 12m odds.

Yields (10y ~4.5%, 30y near 5%) offer attractive carry and a recession hedge, but with the Fed's next move possibly a hike and CPI still ~3.8%, near-term duration risk keeps us off OW; modest up-bias over 12m as the cycle eventually turns.

The dollar is firm on rate support from a hawkish Fed and residual safe-haven demand; cash yields ~3.7-4% with optionality, making USD/cash a high-Sharpe holding while the CPI/Fed and geopolitical tails stay unresolved.
